name: Shimmer
one_liner: Shimmer offers weekly one-to-one video coaching for adults with ADHD or ADHD-like struggles, with an app for check-ins between sessions.
best_for: Adults with ADHD (diagnosed or not) who want a regular coach to help with planning, routines and follow-through
People already treated for ADHD who want practical support alongside medication or therapy
People who can pay out of pocket and prefer video sessions
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need an ADHD diagnosis or medication; coaches are not clinicians and cannot diagnose or prescribe
People who need insurance to cover care; Shimmer does not bill insurance
short_description: Weekly one-to-one video ADHD coaching with an app for goals and check-ins. Self-pay subscription, no diagnosis needed.
long_description: Shimmer is an ADHD coaching service for adults in the US. You are matched with a coach and meet by video each week (30-minute and longer plans), set goals, and use the Shimmer app between sessions for check-ins and reminders; it also has an AI assistant called Indy. You do not need a formal diagnosis. Coaching is not therapy or medical care: coaches do not diagnose or prescribe. It is self-pay; Shimmer does not bill insurance. The company reports internal improvements on ADHD rating scales from member surveys, but we found no peer-reviewed study of Shimmer itself.

pricing.notes: Shimmer's cost page lists $230 a month for weekly 30-minute one-to-one coaching (about $58 per session); app stores list $229.99/month with a first-month discount. Longer (45-minute) plans cost more. First-month refund if requested within 30 days. Not billed to insurance.

privacy.notes: Says it is not a HIPAA covered entity but treats health information as sensitive and does not share coaching sessions with employers or schools; we could not confirm its terms on selling, ad sharing or deletion.

patient_summary: You sign up, get matched with an ADHD coach, and meet by video once a week to work on goals like routines, planning and follow-through, with app check-ins in between. You pay a monthly subscription yourself; insurance is not billed. Coaching does not replace an ADHD evaluation, medication or therapy.
